title: Burgruine Rattenberg
highlights: Medieval castle fortress occupying the Schlossberg above Austria's smallest city
Originally founded in the 10th century by the powerful Bishops of Regensburg
Spectacular vantage point overlooking the historic glassblowers' town and the Inn river
Atmospheric open-air venue hosting the acclaimed traditional Rattenberg Castle Plays
kurzbeschreibung: The Burgruine Rattenberg is perched on the Schlossberg above Austria's smallest town and serves as an open-air stage.
beschreibung:
Schlossberg above Austria's Smallest Town

The Burgruine Rattenberg looms over the historic glassblowing town of Rattenberg from a steep rocky spur above the Inn. Founded as early as the 10th century as a stronghold of the bishops of Regensburg, the castle was later expanded by Herzog Heinrich dem Löwen and the Tyrolean sovereigns.

Culture and Panorama

From the medieval town centre, a short and picturesque walk leads up to the Schlossberg. Alongside the historic remnants of walls, the site offers a wonderful view across the colourful rooftops of the old town. Every summer, the castle courtyard transforms into the atmospheric open-air theatre for the renowned Schlossbergspiele Rattenberg.
